title: Postharvest Deviation Containment, Facts and Process Timeline

content.overview: A postharvest deviation investigation begins by protecting material and evidence. Technician II establishes lot identity, location, timeline, product condition, room/process history and what was actually observed before deciding what caused the condition or what should happen to the product.

vocabulary.definition: A controlled action that prevents uncertain or potentially affected material from being mixed, moved or released while evidence is evaluated.
The documented observations, measurements, identities and events known before causal interpretation.
A chronological record connecting process events, movements, measurements and observations.

sections.title: Contain first when identity or condition is uncertain
sections.body: Protect affected or potentially affected material using the authorized hold/segregation process. Do not blend uncertain material into normal product to make the exception disappear.

sections.title: Build the chronology before the cause story
sections.body: Record harvest/transfer times, rack or container identity, room history, product observations, sampling and movements. Facts that contradict the leading hypothesis remain part of the record.

sections.title: Do not convert containment into disposition
sections.body: Holding material protects evidence and product while the authorized role evaluates release, rework, destruction or other disposition. Technician II does not gain disposition authority from recognizing the deviation.

workedExamples: A suspect rack is placed on hold and identified without moving neighboring unaffected racks into the same status until genealogy and process evidence are checked.
An unusual product condition is documented with time, position and original measurements before staff speculate about a room excursion.
commonMistakes: Declaring the entire facility affected before tracing scope.
Blending questionable material into normal lots.
Writing the cause into the record before the facts are assembled.
Treating a hold as authorization to dispose product.
content.practicalApplication: Create a deviation fact sheet containing lot/rack identity, location, process timeline, product observations, room data, current containment and a separate hypotheses section.
content.summary: Containment protects product and evidence; chronology and facts come before causal and disposition conclusions.

primaryVisuals.title: Containment and fact baseline before causal conclusions
primaryVisuals.alt: Postharvest deviation workflow starting with exact material identity and containment, then preserving the event timeline, product observations, room or process history and current status before hypotheses or disposition decisions are considered.
primaryVisuals.caption: Containment protects product and evidence; it does not decide disposition. Establish lot identity, chronology and observed facts before writing a causal story.
